implementation_notes: The JDK ships the queue: BlockingQueue.put/take cover the blocking producer/consumer pair, offer/poll with timeouts give the bounded waits, and drainTo moves a whole batch into another collection for per-tick aggregation. What replaces the classic structure is the interface plus its happens-before guarantees - the queue type is the synchronization boundary, so payloads published through put are safely visible after take. Choose this variant whenever producers and the drain are different threads.
pitfalls: put/take throw InterruptedException: swallowing it (or not restoring the interrupt flag) breaks shutdown, and an unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue never applies back-pressure - memory grows instead.
drainTo and the bulk Collection methods are not atomic with respect to concurrent producers, and size()/contains() are only approximations under concurrency.
The happens-before edge exists only through the concurrent queue: a hand-rolled ArrayDeque shared between threads is a data race even when individual references look atomic.

variants.name: ArrayDeque drained in the owner thread (single-threaded)
variants.implementation_notes: When the drain runs on the same thread that enqueues - a game loop, an actor mailbox owned by one thread, a UI thread - a plain ArrayDeque with addLast and pollFirst is faster than any concurrent queue: no locks, no CAS, no synchronization at all, and the pending window is directly inspectable for coalescing. What replaces the classic structure is simply the deque plus the drain point; the trade is that the queue must never escape to another thread without explicit synchronization.
pitfalls: ArrayDeque is explicitly not thread-safe: publishing it to another thread without external synchronization is a data race, so cross-thread hand-off is exactly what the BlockingQueue variant is for.
A handler that enqueues into the same deque makes the drain loop unbounded - cap the work per tick or route re-posts to the next tick.
Iterators are fail-fast: removing entries through the deque while an iterator is active throws ConcurrentModificationException, so drain with pollFirst rather than a for-each loop.
